_comment: World scale and cover class for every street prop. The PNGs are all 192x288 because fitclip normalises each asset to its own cell for fidelity — which means the file size says nothing about how big the thing is. A fire hydrant and a burnt-out car are the same pixels on disk. This file is the seam that fixes that: heightM is the object's real height in metres, and the renderer scales from it. A person is 1.8m and draws at UNIT_H = 18px on a 32x16 tile (js/render.js), so px = 18 * heightM / 1.8.
_cover: none = no protection, low = half cover, full = blocks line of sight
_origin: The first eight (crate..bench) are the cut of references/prop-sheet-1.png and were sized by eye before this file existed; they carry heightM now so there is ONE source for how big a prop draws. js/render.js mirrors heightM into PROP_H and test/smoke.mjs fails if the mirror and this file disagree.
_scale: px = SPRITE_H * heightM / 1.8. A person draws at SPRITE_H (js/render.js), not at UNIT_H — UNIT_H is the procedural fallback's height and stopped being the size of a body when units got real plates. And the renderer scales by the plate's INK box, not its file: these cells are padded differently (carwreck fills 44% of its frame, hydrant 96%), so naturalHeight would draw the car at less than half the size this file says it is.
